subject: SLA boundary & tenant-controlled infra — Galileo Systems
messages:
From: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@galileosystems.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Galileo Systems Legal <legal@galileosystems.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T09:11:00-07:00
Subject: SLA boundary & tenant-controlled infra — Galileo Systems

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this. Quick context: we are preparing to go live with Redwood Private in our primary data centers (tenant-managed gateways). Our security and ops teams require the SLA to reflect the fact that parts of the stack are customer-controlled (on-prem gateways, WAN links we manage), and therefore we need a carve-out/exception for latency and availability where our network or on-prem infra are the root cause.

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood accept a shared-responsibility clause that excludes customer-controlled networking and on-prem gateway availability from the uptime calculation?
- If yes, can you provide a short amendment to the Master Services Agreement (MSA) we can run through legal?
- We also need to understand what telemetry Redwood requires to validate incidents (packet captures, agent logs, sampling windows).

Attached a network topology PDF to show where our edge gateways sit.

We'd like to get this resolved before our internal compliance review on 2026-08-10. Best time for a short call this week would be Thursday afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Samantha Reed
Head of Cloud Ops
Galileo Systems
Attachment: network-topology.pdf (diagram, 2 pages)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@galileosystems.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA boundary & tenant-controlled infra — Galileo Systems

Hi Samantha,

Appreciate the topology and clear asks. Short answers up front: yes, we can accept a shared-responsibility model in principle — with a narrowly scoped amendment that enumerates excluded components (customer-controlled WAN, on-prem gateway processes, and customer-managed DNS). We will also need a reliable way to determine causality for incidents (Redwood-side vs customer-side) so the amendment includes agreed observability signals and escalation playbook steps.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll loop in Legal and Product with a one-page amendment draft (we typically keep the language bulletized for clarity).
2) Please confirm the telemetry you can reasonably share (syslog, agent diagnostic bundle, packet captures) and retention windows.
3) Pick a 30-min slot Thursday 2026-08-05 2:00–2:30pm PT and I’ll send a calendar invite.

I’m CC'ing Vivek (networking product) to take a quick look at required signals.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: draft amendment for Galileo — please review

Vivek / Laura,

Posting the draft language below for quick review before I send to Samantha. I tried to keep it tight and observable-focused to avoid broad carve-outs. Attached is a doc with the same text for redline.

DRAFT AMENDMENT (summary form):
1) Excluded Components: For the purposes of calculating Redwood’s Service Availability SLA, the following are agreed to be Customer-Controlled Components and are excluded from uptime calculations: (i) Customer-managed on-prem gateway appliances and virtual gateways; (ii) Customer-controlled WAN/transit links outside Redwood-managed networks; (iii) DNS or routing configurations under Customer control.

2) Causality & Evidence: Incidents affecting availability/latency will be investigated using mutually agreed evidence types. If Redwood demonstrates, based on at least two distinct telemetry sources (e.g., Redwood agent logs + BGP session diagnostics), that the root cause is within Redwood’s infrastructure, Redwood remains responsible. If evidence shows the root cause lies within the Customer-Controlled Components, the incident will be excluded from SLA uptime calculations.

3) Evidence Types & Retention: Customer agrees to provide, upon request and subject to any regulatory/privacy restrictions, diagnostic bundles including syslog extracts, packet captures for implicated flows, and agent traces for a 72-hour window around the incident. Redwood will retain relevant service logs for a 30-day window for investigation purposes.

4) Escalation & Validation: For disputed incidents, both parties will engage a joint incident validation call within 24 hours of request. If unresolved, an independent third-party reviewer (mutually agreed) will examine the evidence and issue a binding determination for SLA credit eligibility. Cost of the third-party review shall be borne by the losing party.

Notes / questions: 
- Laura: legal, does the third-party reviewer clause introduce any procurement/insurance concerns?
- Vivek: from an instrumentation perspective, do we need to add any specific agent-side IDs or sampling settings so logs are correlatable?

Attachments: galileo-sla-proposed-amendment.docx

Olga

From: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@galileosystems.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Galileo Systems Legal <legal@galileosystems.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T17:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA boundary & tenant-controlled infra — Galileo Systems

Olga,

Thanks — the draft looks reasonable and narrowly scoped, which is exactly what our legal/compliance team wanted to see. We ran it by Legal; they suggested one small addition to the Evidence Types clause to call out "retained flow-sampled PCAPs at 1:1000" as an example of acceptable packet sampling for non-production incidents. They also approved the joint validation + third-party reviewer approach.

We attach an initial signed memorandum of agreement (MOA) draft for Redwood to review; it includes the amendment embedded (see signed-moa-draft.pdf). We can accept the proposed language pending Redwood confirmation on two items:
- Redwood agrees to keep a 30-day retention window for correlated service logs (as you proposed).
- Redwood confirms the procedure and contact for requesting diagnostic bundles (SOP + contact email).

We are available for a short call tomorrow 2026-08-05 2pm PT to finalize. If you can confirm the SOP and the retention commitment in writing ahead of the call, Legal can issue a countersigned MOA quickly.

Best regards,
Samantha Reed
Head of Cloud Ops
Galileo Systems
Attachment: signed-moa-draft.pdf
